title: Legal document confidentiality for paralegals on Mac: how to protect client data securely
metaTitle: Legal document confidentiality for paralegals on Mac
description: Learn how to maintain legal document confidentiality on your Mac. Discover simple security habits, technical fixes, and how to protect sensitive client data effectively.
intro: Legal document confidentiality is the bedrock of your work as a paralegal. Maintaining strict data security on your Mac is essential to protect client privacy and firm reputation.
tldr: Enable FileVault to encrypt your entire Mac drive.
Use strong, unique passwords for every legal application.
Always lock your screen when you step away from your desk.
Enable multi-factor authentication on all cloud-based legal tools.
Back up files only to encrypted locations like authorized cloud storage.

blocks.text: Why legal document confidentiality is at risk
Your Mac is a gateway to sensitive information. Paralegals handle high volumes of data that attract cyber threats. You face risks from phishing, weak passwords, and accidental data exposure.
Many firms use remote work setups. This expands the area where data can be intercepted. You must be vigilant when accessing case files outside the office network.
Core security settings for your Mac
Start by securing your hardware. macOS has built-in tools that provide strong protection. Always follow your firm policy regarding data storage and encryption.

items: FileVault: Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security > FileVault to encrypt your disk.
Lock Screen: Set your Mac to require a password immediately after the screen saver starts. Use System Settings > Lock Screen.
Firewall: Turn on the firewall in System Settings > Network > Firewall to block unwanted incoming connections.
Standard Account: Do not use an administrator account for daily tasks. Create a standard account in System Settings > Users & Groups.

blocks.text: Sharing files is part of your daily routine. Use secure methods only. Avoid sending unencrypted documents via standard email if they contain highly sensitive data.
Always check if your firm has a preferred secure file transfer service before sending attachments. If not, ask your IT department for a secure alternative.

faq.question: How do I know if my Mac is encrypted?
faq.answer: Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security. Look for FileVault. If it says On, your drive is encrypted.

faq.question: Should I use public Wi-Fi for legal work?
faq.answer: No. Public Wi-Fi is insecure. Use a firm-approved VPN if you must work outside the office.

fixes.title: Enable FileVault
fixes.text: Encrypt your hard drive so that data is unreadable if the Mac is stolen.

fixes.title: Use a password manager
fixes.text: Generate and store unique, complex passwords for every legal tool you use.

fixes.title: Lock your screen
fixes.text: Press ⌃ ⌘ Q to instantly lock your Mac whenever you leave your desk.
